title: A Thorn for the Ember Revisited
premise: Petra Okonkwo has spent six years as the Ember Court's royal food-taster, swallowing poison so kings can eat, and slipping through the Thornfell passes as a courier for smugglers who pay better than the crown. When a scholar's auction reveals a century-old prophecy book naming 'the taster of thorns' as the only one who can unbind King Aldric from the ember-spirit that has worn his crown—and his will—for a generation, Petra's carefully invisible life ignites. Hunted by the spirit's loyalists and betrayed by the mentor who raised them, Petra must choose between loyalty to the court that owns them and the truth that could free it, discovering along the way that they are the prophecy's author's last descendant, inheriting both the gift of immunity and the duty it demands. In the end, Petra swallows the ember itself, binding the spirit into their own body rather than the king's, trading their invisibility for a visible, painful place at the heart of a kingdom reborn.
about_author: I. M. Blackwood is the pen name of a former line cook turned fantasy novelist who claims to have tasted everything once and regretted most of it. They write from a mountain cabin where the roads are bad on purpose.

chapters.title: The Taster's Oath
chapters.summary: POV Petra. A routine tasting at the Ember Court goes wrong when Petra detects nightshade in the king's stew—planted by someone inside the kitchen. The emotional beat: quiet competence masking loneliness; Petra realizes someone wants the king dead, or wants them noticed.

chapters.title: Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: POV Petra. On a courier run through the Thornfell passes, Petra trades gossip with smuggler allies and learns strange caravans have been buying old books and relics. Beat: warmth of found family among outlaws, contrasted with the cold formality of court.

chapters.title: A Date with Dust
chapters.summary: POV Petra. At an archive auction, Petra meets scholar Yew Andrade over a disputed lot—a prophecy book written a century ago. Flipping its pages, Petra finds tonight's date, their own description, and the words 'the taster of thorns.' Beat: vertigo; the floor drops out of an ordinary life.

chapters.title: What Wears the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Researching with Yew, Petra learns King Aldric was 'bound' twenty years ago to an ember-spirit after a plague nearly ended the dynasty. Every decree since bears the same scorch-marked signature. Beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Poisoner's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Tracing the nightshade, Petra finds Master Taster Sefu's private ledger—entries in their own handwriting they never wrote, dated years ahead. Beat: betrayal and confusion; the person who raised them may be scripting their fate.

chapters.title: Invisible No More
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Court spymaster Lady Vess summons Petra, revealing she knows about the prophecy book and offers protection—in exchange for destroying it. Beat: the trap of being seen; safety offered at the price of truth.

chapters.title: Thornfell Road at Night
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Fleeing with the book through smuggler routes, Petra is ambushed by crown loyalists who shouldn't know the paths. Smuggler friend Rook dies covering their escape. Beat: grief; the cost of belonging made literal.

chapters.title: The Author's Grave
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Following clues in the margins, Petra reaches a hermitage and the tomb of Ilsa Okonkwo—the prophet, and Petra's great-great-grandmother. A hidden letter reveals the immunity in Petra's blood is inherited, cultivated for this purpose. Beat: inheritance as burden and gift.

chapters.title: Audience with Ash
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Summoned before King Aldric, Petra watches him fight the ember-spirit for control of his own tongue mid-sentence. He whispers 'unbind me' before the flame reasserts. Beat: horror and compassion entwined.

chapters.title: Sefu's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Confronting Sefu, Petra learns he wrote the forged ledger entries under Vess's orders to discredit any true heir to the prophecy. He begs forgiveness; Petra cannot yet give it. Beat: anger tempered by love for a flawed father-figure.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Ilsa's letter details the rite: the unbinding requires a willing vessel of Okonkwo blood to swallow the ember whole. Petra begins training their body to hold what no throat should carry. Beat: grim resolve; agency claimed over destiny.

chapters.title: Yew's Heresy
chapters.summary: POV Yew. The scholar's chapter: Yew deciphers that the prophecy names two endings—one where the taster frees the king, one where the taster becomes the next bound thing. Yew hides this from Petra. Beat: guilt; loyalty beginning to war with truth.

chapters.title: Court of Cinders
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Vess moves openly now, arresting smugglers and burning prophecy copies. Petra returns undercover as a penitent taster to reach the king's side. Beat: tension of walking back into the lion's mouth wearing a mask.

chapters.title: The Second Poisoning
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Another assassination attempt—this time aimed at Petra, using a compound engineered to burn out their immunity. Sefu takes the cup meant for them and dies in agony. Beat: devastating loss; the debt of protection repaid too late for thanks.

chapters.title: Emberfall
chapters.summary: POV Petra. With Sefu dead and Vess blaming Petra for treason, the court turns. Petra escapes through the kitchens with help from a kitchen girl who owes them nothing and gives everything. Beat: unexpected solidarity; hope kindled in small hands.

chapters.title: The Thing Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: POV Petra. In the deep vaults, Petra finds the original binding circle and learns the ember-spirit was once the kingdom's guardian, corrupted by Vess's predecessors who fed it fear to keep power. Beat: the enemy reframed; systems, not monsters, are the true villain.

chapters.title: Truth in the Throne Room
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Petra exposes Vess before the assembled court, presenting the ledgers, the letter, and the scorched signatures. Vess counters by revealing Yew's hidden second ending. Beat: public rupture; trust shattered at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Choice of Thorns
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Cornered, Petra must choose: flee with Yew and live hidden forever, or perform the rite knowing either outcome costs them everything. They choose the rite. Beat: the thematic crux—loyalty and truth finally pointing the same direction.

chapters.title: Swallowing the Sun
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Before the court, Petra drinks the ember from the broken crown. Agony, transformation, and the spirit's voice inside them offering the same bargain Aldric accepted. Beat: climax of body and will; refusal of the bargain.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: POV Aldric. The freed king's chapter: Aldric, lucid for the first time in twenty years, executes the counter-binding Ilsa designed, chaining the spirit not to a person but to the land itself. Beat: catharsis; two captives freed by one sacrifice.

chapters.title: A Visible Life
chapters.summary: POV Petra. Recovering but changed—ember-veined, immune to poison and to anonymity both—Petra declines a title, instead founding a school for tasters and healers. Yew stays; Rook's smuggler road becomes a sanctioned trade route. Beat: bittersweet renewal; belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: The Last Page Burns
chapters.summary: POV Petra. One year later, Petra burns the prophecy book's final page—which had shown a future they've already altered—and writes their own first entry in a new book. Beat: resolution; inheritance transformed from fate into authorship.
